subproblem.title: Measurability and unit bounds of |D^⊥r|² = normalRadialSq (Simon 6.1, step 7(b))
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, V a rectifiable n-varifold in E (RectifiableVarifold n ℓ) with weight μ = V.weight, and ξ ∈ E. Assume that x ↦ p_x := (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection, a map E → (E →L[ℝ] E), is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Then q(x) := V.normalRadialSq ξ x = |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)|²/|x − ξ|² (p_x^⊥ the orthogonal projection onto (T_xV)^⊥, division by 0 giving 0) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and 0 ≤ q(x) ≤ 1 for every x ∈ E.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (V : RectifiableVarifold n ℓ) (ξ : Ambient n ℓ), AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x ↦ (V.tangentSpace x).starProjection) V.weight → AEStronglyMeasurable (fun x ↦ V.normalRadialSq ξ x) V.weight ∧ ∀ x, 0 ≤ V.normalRadialSq ξ x ∧ V.normalRadialSq ξ x ≤ 1
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. T_x := V.tangentSpace x, p_x := T_x.starProjection and p_x^⊥ := (T_x)ᗮ.starProjection (orthogonal projections, continuous linear maps E → E); μ := V.weight. By definition V.normalRadialSq ξ x = |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)|² / |x − ξ|², with real division (a/0 = 0). This is step 7(b) of the parent proof together with the bound 0 ≤ q ≤ 1 stated in the parent's conventions.

1. For every subspace T of the finite-dimensional space E, the orthogonal projection onto T^⊥ equals id − p_T (Mathlib Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal': Tᗮ.starProjection = 1 − T.starProjection). Hence x ↦ p_x^⊥ is the map x ↦ 1 − p_x, the difference of a constant map and the μ-a.e. strongly measurable map x ↦ p_x; so x ↦ p_x^⊥ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.

2. Evaluation (L, v) ↦ L v is a continuous bilinear map (E →L[ℝ] E) × E → E (Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.apply, used through ContinuousLinearMap.aestronglyMeasurable_comp₂). The map x ↦ x − ξ is continuous, hence μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Therefore x ↦ p_x^⊥(x − ξ) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.

3. Composing with the continuous maps v ↦ |v| and s ↦ s², the map x ↦ |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)|² is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. The map x ↦ (|x − ξ|²)⁻¹ is Borel measurable (inversion ℝ → ℝ is measurable and x ↦ |x − ξ|² is continuous), hence μ-a.e. strongly measurable (ℝ is second countable). The product x ↦ |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)|² · (|x − ξ|²)⁻¹ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable, and it equals q(x) for every x, because a/b = a·b⁻¹ for all real a, b (including b = 0, where both sides are 0). Hence q is μ-a.e. strongly measurable.

4. Lower bound. For every x, the numerator |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)|² and the denominator |x − ξ|² are ≥ 0, and a quotient of nonnegative reals is ≥ 0; so q(x) ≥ 0.

5. Upper bound. If x = ξ then x − ξ = 0 and q(x) = 0/0 = 0 ≤ 1. If x ≠ ξ then |x − ξ|² > 0; orthogonal projections do not increase norms (Mathlib Submodule.norm_starProjection_apply_le), so |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)| ≤ |x − ξ|, hence |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)|² ≤ |x − ξ|² and q(x) ≤ 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: p_x^⊥ = 1 − p_x (Submodule.starProjection_orthogonal'), so x ↦ p_x^⊥ is μ-a.e. strongly measurable
x ↦ p_x^⊥(x − ξ) is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (continuous bilinear evaluation of an a.e.-measurable operator field at the continuous field x − ξ)
q(x) = |p_x^⊥(x − ξ)|² · (|x − ξ|²)⁻¹ pointwise, a product of a.e.-strongly measurable functions
0 ≤ q ≤ 1: nonnegative quotient; q(ξ) = 0; |p_x^⊥ v| ≤ |v| for x ≠ ξ

audit.reason: The proposition exactly matches the stated projection-measurability hypothesis and pointwise bounds. The proof correctly uses the continuous-linear-map identity p_perp = id − p, continuous evaluation, measurable real inversion and multiplication. It treats the zero denominator separately and derives the upper bound from contraction of orthogonal projection. No tangent-dimension assumption or parent theorem is silently required; the proof is complete.

subproblem.title: Cutoff, radial profile and radial test field outside a ball (Simon 6.1, steps 2–4)
subproblem.statement: Let n, ℓ ∈ ℕ and E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ} (Euclidean). Let K ⊆ E be compact, ξ ∈ E, R ≥ 0 and ε > 0. Then there exist ζ: E → ℝ and γ: ℝ → ℝ such that: (i) ζ ∈ C¹(E); (ii) ζ(x) = 1 and ∇ζ(x) = 0 (Mathlib gradient) for every x ∈ K; (iii) γ ∈ C¹(ℝ); (iv) γ(t) ≥ 0 and γ'(t) ≥ 0 for every t ≥ 0, where γ' = deriv γ; (v) γ(t) = 0 for 0 ≤ t ≤ R + ε; (vi) γ(t) > 0 for every t > R + ε; (vii) X(x) := (ζ(x)γ(|x − ξ|))(x − ξ) is a test field in U := E ∖ B_R(ξ) (B_R(ξ) = closedBall ξ R): X is C¹, has compact support, and tsupport X ⊆ U (IsTestField (closedBall ξ R)ᶜ X).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (K : Set (Ambient n ℓ)) (ξ : Ambient n ℓ) (R ε : ℝ), IsCompact K → 0 ≤ R → 0 < ε → ∃ (ζ : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (γ : ℝ → ℝ), ContDiff ℝ 1 ζ ∧ (∀ x ∈ K, ζ x = 1 ∧ gradient ζ x = 0) ∧ ContDiff ℝ 1 γ ∧ (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → 0 ≤ γ t ∧ 0 ≤ deriv γ t) ∧ (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ R + ε → γ t = 0) ∧ (∀ t : ℝ, R + ε < t → 0 < γ t) ∧ IsTestField (closedBall ξ R)ᶜ (fun x ↦ (ζ x * γ ‖x - ξ‖) • (x - ξ))
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. B(ξ, ρ) = ball ξ ρ is the open ball and B_ρ(ξ) = closedBall ξ ρ the closed ball; |·| is the Euclidean norm; ∇f(x) = gradient f x is the Riesz representative of the Fréchet derivative Df(x) (the image of Df(x) under the inverse of the linear isometric equivalence toDual); IsTestField U X means X is C¹ (ContDiff ℝ 1 X), HasCompactSupport X and tsupport X ⊆ U. This is steps 2–4 of the parent proof (Simon 6.1), with W := B(ξ, ρ₀) in step 2 and the radial profile of option (i) of the parent's step-3 remark.

1. Choice of W. K is compact, hence bounded, so there is ρ ∈ ℝ with K ⊆ B(ξ, ρ). Put ρ₀ := |ρ| + 1 > 0 and W := B(ξ, ρ₀). W is open and K ⊆ B(ξ, ρ) ⊆ W because ρ ≤ |ρ| < ρ₀.

2. The cutoff ζ. E is a finite-dimensional real inner product space, so it has smooth bump functions (Mathlib HasContDiffBump). Let f be the bump function centred at ξ with inner radius rIn = ρ₀ and outer radius rOut = ρ₀ + 1 (Mathlib ContDiffBump ξ; the requirements 0 < rIn < rOut hold). Then f is C^∞ (ContDiffBump.contDiff), f(x) = 1 for every x ∈ B_{ρ₀}(ξ) (ContDiffBump.one_of_mem_closedBall), and f has compact support (ContDiffBump.hasCompactSupport). Put ζ := f. In particular ζ ∈ C¹(E), which is (i).

3. Property (ii). Let x ∈ K. Then x ∈ W, W is open and W ⊆ B_{ρ₀}(ξ), so ζ ≡ 1 on the neighbourhood W of x. Hence ζ(x) = 1, and since ζ agrees with the constant function 1 on a neighbourhood of x, Dζ(x) = D(const 1)(x) = 0 (Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq, fderiv_const). The gradient is the image of Dζ(x) under a linear map, so ∇ζ(x) = 0.

4. The profile γ. Put c := R + ε; then c > 0 because R ≥ 0 and ε > 0. Let g := expNegInvGlue, i.e. g(s) = 0 for s ≤ 0 and g(s) = exp(−1/s) for s > 0. Mathlib provides: g ∈ C^∞(ℝ) (expNegInvGlue.contDiff), g is monotone (expNegInvGlue.monotone), g(s) ≥ 0 for all s (expNegInvGlue.nonneg), g(s) = 0 for s ≤ 0 (expNegInvGlue.zero_of_nonpos) and g(s) > 0 for s > 0 (expNegInvGlue.pos_of_pos). Define γ(t) := g(t² − c²). As the composition of the C^∞ map g with the polynomial t ↦ t² − c², γ is C^∞, in particular γ ∈ C¹(ℝ), which is (iii).

5. Property (iv). γ(t) = g(t² − c²) ≥ 0 for every t. By the chain rule (g is differentiable everywhere and t ↦ t² − c² has derivative 2t), γ'(t) = g'(t² − c²)·2t for every t ∈ ℝ. A monotone function ℝ → ℝ has nonnegative derivative at every point (Monotone.deriv_nonneg), so g'(s) ≥ 0 for every s. Hence γ'(t) ≥ 0 for every t ≥ 0.

6. Property (v). If 0 ≤ t ≤ c then t² ≤ c², i.e. t² − c² ≤ 0, so γ(t) = g(t² − c²) = 0.

7. Property (vi). If t > c then t > c > 0, so t² > c², i.e. t² − c² > 0, and γ(t) = g(t² − c²) > 0.

8. Property (vii): X is C¹. For every x ∈ E, γ(|x − ξ|) = g(|x − ξ|² − c²). The map x ↦ |x − ξ|² is C^∞ on E (the squared Euclidean norm is C^∞, Mathlib contDiff_norm_sq, composed with the affine map x ↦ x − ξ), so x ↦ γ(|x − ξ|) = g(|x − ξ|² − c²) is C^∞ on E; no differentiability of the norm at ξ is needed. Hence the scalar function x ↦ ζ(x)γ(|x − ξ|) is C¹ (product of C¹ functions), and X(x) = (ζ(x)γ(|x − ξ|))·(x − ξ) is C¹ (scalar multiplication is a continuous bilinear map and x ↦ x − ξ is C^∞).

9. Property (vii): compact support. If X(x) ≠ 0 then the scalar factor ζ(x)γ(|x − ξ|) is nonzero, so ζ(x) ≠ 0. Thus supp X ⊆ supp ζ, and since ζ has compact support, X has compact support (HasCompactSupport.mono).

10. Property (vii): tsupport X ⊆ U. Let F_c := {x ∈ E : |x − ξ| ≥ c}; it is closed, being the preimage of [c, ∞) under the continuous map x ↦ |x − ξ|. If |x − ξ| < c then γ(|x − ξ|) = 0 by (v) (applied to t = |x − ξ| ≥ 0), hence X(x) = 0; therefore supp X ⊆ F_c. As F_c is closed, tsupport X = closure(supp X) ⊆ F_c. Finally F_c ⊆ U: if |x − ξ| ≥ c = R + ε > R then x ∉ B_R(ξ). Hence tsupport X ⊆ U.

11. Steps 2–10 provide ζ and γ satisfying (i)–(vii). ∎
proof_key_steps: K ⊆ W := B(ξ, ρ₀) with ρ₀ = |ρ| + 1 > 0; ζ := ContDiffBump at ξ with rIn = ρ₀, rOut = ρ₀ + 1 (C^∞, compactly supported, ζ = 1 on B_{ρ₀}(ξ) ⊇ W)
For x ∈ K, ζ ≡ 1 on the open set W ∋ x, so ζ(x) = 1, Dζ(x) = 0 and ∇ζ(x) = 0
γ(t) := expNegInvGlue(t² − (R + ε)²) is C^∞, γ ≥ 0, γ'(t) = 2t·g'(t² − (R + ε)²) ≥ 0 for t ≥ 0 (g monotone), γ = 0 on [0, R + ε], γ > 0 on (R + ε, ∞)
x ↦ γ(|x − ξ|) = g(|x − ξ|² − (R + ε)²) is C^∞, so X = (ζ·γ(|· − ξ|))·(· − ξ) is C¹; supp X ⊆ supp ζ gives compact support
supp X ⊆ {|x − ξ| ≥ R + ε} (closed) ⊆ E ∖ B_R(ξ), hence tsupport X ⊆ U

audit.reason: The prose and exact Lean proposition agree on every hypothesis and conclusion. The supplied proof constructs the bump and squared-radius expNegInvGlue profile, proves the gradient vanishes on K, checks all profile properties, and establishes smoothness, compact support and support containment for the field. It handles the centre without differentiating the norm and covers empty K and zero-dimensional ambient spaces. This is a complete, non-circular obligation for parent steps 2–4.

subproblem.title: Positivity argument: the radial identity forces spt μ ⊆ B_{R+ε}(ξ) (Simon 6.1, steps 7–9)
subproblem.statement: Let n ≥ 1 and ℓ be natural numbers, E = Ambient n ℓ = ℝ^{n+ℓ}, μ a measure on (the Borel σ-algebra of) E that is finite on compact sets (IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ) and whose support spt μ = μ.support is compact. Let H: E → E, q: E → ℝ, γ: ℝ → ℝ, ξ ∈ E, R ≥ 0, ε > 0, U := E ∖ B_R(ξ) (B_R(ξ) = closedBall ξ R) and r = r(x) := |x − ξ|. Assume: H is locally μ-integrable on U (LocallyIntegrableOn H U μ); q is μ-a.e. strongly measurable and 0 ≤ q(x) ≤ 1 for every x; γ ∈ C¹(ℝ); γ(t) ≥ 0 and γ'(t) ≥ 0 for every t ≥ 0 (γ' = deriv γ); γ(t) = 0 for 0 ≤ t ≤ R + ε; γ(t) > 0 for every t > R + ε; (C) |⟨H(x), x − ξ⟩| < n for μ-a.e. x ∈ U; and (★★) ∫_U [nγ(r) + rγ'(r)(1 − q(x))] dμ(x) = −∫_U γ(r)⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩ dμ(x) (Bochner integrals with respect to μ restricted to U). Then spt μ ⊆ B_{R+ε}(ξ).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n ℓ : ℕ) (μ : Measure (Ambient n ℓ)) (H : Ambient n ℓ → Ambient n ℓ) (q : Ambient n ℓ → ℝ) (γ : ℝ → ℝ) (ξ : Ambient n ℓ) (R ε : ℝ), 0 < n → 0 ≤ R → 0 < ε → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → IsCompact μ.support → LocallyIntegrableOn H (closedBall ξ R)ᶜ μ → AEStronglyMeasurable q μ → (∀ x, 0 ≤ q x ∧ q x ≤ 1) → ContDiff ℝ 1 γ → (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → 0 ≤ γ t ∧ 0 ≤ deriv γ t) → (∀ t : ℝ, 0 ≤ t → t ≤ R + ε → γ t = 0) → (∀ t : ℝ, R + ε < t → 0 < γ t) → (∀ᵐ x ∂μ, x ∈ (closedBall ξ R)ᶜ → |inner ℝ (H x) (x - ξ)| < (n : ℝ)) → ∫ x in (closedBall ξ R)ᶜ, ((n : ℝ) * γ ‖x - ξ‖ + ‖x - ξ‖ * deriv γ ‖x - ξ‖ * (1 - q x)) ∂μ = -∫ x in (closedBall ξ R)ᶜ, γ ‖x - ξ‖ * inner ℝ (x - ξ) (H x) ∂μ → μ.support ⊆ closedBall ξ (R + ε)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Conventions. c := R + ε, so c > R ≥ 0. F(x) := nγ(r) + rγ'(r)(1 − q(x)) and G(x) := γ(r)⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩, so (★★) reads ∫_U F dμ = −∫_U G dμ. The real inner product is symmetric (real_inner_comm), so |⟨H(x), x − ξ⟩| = |⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩|. U is open (complement of a closed ball), hence measurable; μ⌞U denotes μ restricted to U. Since a Bochner integral of a non-integrable function is 0 by convention, integrability is established (steps 2–5) before linearity is used. This is steps 7–9 of the parent proof, stated for an abstract measure μ (there μ = μ_V) and an abstract function q (there q = q_ξ = V.normalRadialSq ξ); steps 2–5 are the parent's step 7(a)–(d) and steps 6–7 its steps 8–9.

1. Null complement and a bounding ball. E is second countable, hence hereditarily Lindelöf, so the complement of the support of μ is μ-null: μ(E ∖ spt μ) = 0 (Mathlib Measure.support_mem_ae). Since spt μ is compact it is bounded, so there is ρ₀ > 0 with spt μ ⊆ B(ξ, ρ₀) (open ball).

2. Vanishing off S (parent step 7(a)). Let S := spt μ ∩ {x : r(x) ≥ c}. S is compact (a closed subset of the compact set spt μ), S ⊆ U (because r ≥ c > R on S), and μ(S) < ∞ (μ is finite on compact sets). Let x ∈ spt μ ∖ S. Then 0 ≤ r < c, so γ(r) = 0. Moreover rγ'(r) = 0: if r = 0 the factor r vanishes; if 0 < r < c then γ vanishes on the open interval (0, c), which is a neighbourhood of r, so γ'(r) = 0. Hence F(x) = G(x) = γ(r) = rγ'(r)(1 − q(x)) = γ(r)|⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩| = 0 for every x ∈ spt μ ∖ S. Together with step 1, each of the functions F, G, x ↦ γ(r), x ↦ rγ'(r)(1 − q(x)) and x ↦ γ(r)|⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩| coincides μ-a.e. with its product with the indicator 1_S.

3. Measurability (parent step 7(b)). γ and γ' are continuous because γ ∈ C¹ (ContDiff.continuous_deriv), x ↦ r(x) is continuous, and q is μ-a.e. strongly measurable. Hence F, x ↦ γ(r) and x ↦ rγ'(r)(1 − q(x)) are μ-a.e. strongly measurable (sums and products of a.e.-strongly measurable real functions).

4. Bounds and integrability of the q-terms (parent step 7(c)). Put M₀ := max_{t ∈ [0, ρ₀]} γ(t) and M₁ := max_{t ∈ [0, ρ₀]} tγ'(t) (continuous functions on a compact interval attain their maxima). For x ∈ S we have 0 ≤ r < ρ₀, hence 0 ≤ γ(r) ≤ M₀ and 0 ≤ rγ'(r) ≤ M₁ (using γ ≥ 0 and γ' ≥ 0 on [0, ∞)), and 0 ≤ 1 − q(x) ≤ 1. With step 2 this gives, μ-a.e., |F| ≤ (nM₀ + M₁)1_S, 0 ≤ γ(r) ≤ M₀1_S and 0 ≤ rγ'(r)(1 − q) ≤ M₁1_S. Since μ(S) < ∞, the functions F, x ↦ γ(r) and x ↦ rγ'(r)(1 − q(x)) are μ-integrable (a.e.-strongly measurable by step 3 and dominated by integrable functions), hence μ⌞U-integrable.

5. Integrability of the H-terms (parent step 7(d)). H is μ-integrable on the compact set S ⊆ U because H is locally integrable on U (Mathlib LocallyIntegrableOn.integrableOn_compact_subset); in particular H is a.e. strongly measurable with respect to μ⌞S, and so are x ↦ ⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩ (continuous inner product of a.e.-strongly measurable functions), G and x ↦ γ(r)|⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩|. For x ∈ S, Cauchy–Schwarz gives |⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩| ≤ r|H(x)|, hence |G(x)| ≤ γ(r)·r·|H(x)| ≤ M₀ρ₀|H(x)| and 0 ≤ γ(r)|⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩| ≤ M₀ρ₀|H(x)|. So G and x ↦ γ(r)|⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩| are integrable on S. Since S ⊆ U and both functions vanish μ-a.e. on U ∖ S by step 2, they are μ⌞U-integrable (Mathlib IntegrableOn.of_ae_sdiff_eq_zero).

6. Positivity (parent step 8). By (★★) and linearity of the integral (steps 4 and 5),
n∫_U γ(r) dμ + ∫_U rγ'(r)(1 − q) dμ = ∫_U F dμ = −∫_U G dμ ≤ ∫_U γ(r)|⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩| dμ,
the inequality because −G(x) ≤ γ(r)|⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩| for every x (γ(r) ≥ 0 as r ≥ 0). Since rγ'(r)(1 − q(x)) ≥ 0 for every x (r ≥ 0, γ'(r) ≥ 0, q ≤ 1), ∫_U rγ'(r)(1 − q) dμ ≥ 0, and therefore
∫_U γ(r)(n − |⟨H(x), x − ξ⟩|) dμ ≤ 0,
where the integrand is μ⌞U-integrable as the difference of nγ(r) and γ(r)|⟨x − ξ, H(x)⟩|. By (C) and γ(r) ≥ 0 this integrand is ≥ 0 for μ-a.e. x ∈ U. A μ⌞U-integrable function which is ≥ 0 a.e. and has integral ≤ 0 has integral 0 and vanishes a.e. (Mathlib integral_eq_zero_iff_of_nonneg_ae). Hence γ(r)(n − |⟨H(x), x − ξ⟩|) = 0 for μ-a.e. x ∈ U, and since n − |⟨H(x), x − ξ⟩| > 0 for μ-a.e. x ∈ U by (C), γ(|x − ξ|) = 0 for μ-a.e. x ∈ U.

7. Support (parent step 9). The set O := {x : |x − ξ| > c} is open (preimage of (c, ∞) under a continuous map), O ⊆ U because c > R, and γ(|x − ξ|) > 0 for every x ∈ O. By step 6, μ(O) ≤ μ({x ∈ U : γ(|x − ξ|) ≠ 0}) = 0. Every point of spt μ has all its neighbourhoods of positive measure, so the open μ-null set O is disjoint from spt μ (Mathlib Measure.subset_compl_support_of_isOpen). Hence spt μ ⊆ E ∖ O = B_c(ξ) = B_{R+ε}(ξ). ∎

Formalization note (not part of the argument; the numbered steps above are the proof, and either route proves the same statement): steps 2–4 may be shortened by observing that μ(E) = μ(spt μ) + μ(E ∖ spt μ) < ∞, so μ is a finite measure and F, being a.e.-strongly measurable and bounded on spt μ by max_{spt μ}(n|γ(r)| + |rγ'(r)|), is μ-integrable (Integrable.of_bound, IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn); step 6 may equivalently be run on F + G, which is ≥ γ(r)(n − |⟨x − ξ, H⟩|) + rγ'(r)(1 − q) ≥ 0 μ-a.e. on U and has ∫_U (F + G) dμ = 0 by (★★); step 7 may use Measure.support_subset_of_isClosed with the closed set B_{R+ε}(ξ).
proof_key_steps: μ(E ∖ spt μ) = 0 and spt μ ⊆ B(ξ, ρ₀); S := spt μ ∩ {|x − ξ| ≥ R + ε} is compact, S ⊆ U, μ(S) < ∞
On spt μ ∖ S, γ(r) = rγ'(r) = 0, so every integrand vanishes μ-a.e. off S
F, γ(r), rγ'(r)(1 − q) are a.e.-strongly measurable and dominated by constants times 1_S, hence μ⌞U-integrable; G and γ(r)|⟨x − ξ, H⟩| are μ⌞U-integrable because H ∈ L¹(S)
(★★) and rγ'(r)(1 − q) ≥ 0 give ∫_U γ(r)(n − |⟨H, x − ξ⟩|) dμ ≤ 0 with a.e. nonnegative integrand, so γ(|x − ξ|) = 0 μ-a.e. on U
The open set {|x − ξ| > R + ε} ⊆ U is μ-null, hence disjoint from spt μ, so spt μ ⊆ B_{R+ε}(ξ)

audit.reason: Every measure, curvature, profile, q and radial-identity hypothesis is present in both prose and Lean. The proof establishes vanishing off the compact set S, measurability and integrability before using integral linearity, then uses the strict curvature bound to force gamma to vanish almost everywhere. The open-null-set argument gives exactly the stated support containment. The almost-everywhere implication matches restriction to the measurable open exterior. The argument is complete and non-circular, and its conclusion supplies the parent's epsilon-ball bound.
